info.bio: Hablar de este grupo es hablar del comienzo de la música jamaicana moderna. Luego de la independencia de la isla caribeña en 1962, un ritmo se apropió de la efervescencia del acontecimiento: el Ska, mezcla de Rhythm & Blues, Mento, Jazz y música Afro Cubana, fue el emblema de la nueva nación. Este estilo aún continúa vigente en la música moderna de Jamaica, y fue el propulsor de otros géneros como el Reggae, Dub, Rocksteady, Drum´nBass, Acid jazz.

scenes.name: Ska y rocksteady en Londres
scenes.author: Jon Savage
scenes.desc: Savage dejó fuera el ska por la casi imposibilidad de fechar los discos, pero estaba en todas partes: Peter Meaden veía en 1964 un movimiento mod que solo tenía pop americano, R&B y «una pizca de ska jamaicano»; Island editó desde 1963 una avalancha de ska y Chris Blackwell diversificó con Sue; en Le Duce y en Tiles sonaban Prince Buster, Desmond Dekker o los Wailers, y en Tiles el ska llegó a dominar: «cualquiera podía bailar un disco de ska», y por primera vez la juventud negra se mezclaba en los clubes. La discografía del libro recoge algunos sencillos del año.

podcast.title: The Skatalites (Jamaica, 1963–1967) – Trombone-Led Studio Band; Played on Virtually Every Jamaican Record; Don Drummond Murdered His Girlfriend; Died in Asylum 1969
podcast.body: Don Drummond was a trombone player who gave Jamaican ska a slightly darker feel. He first called his group The Satellites, then changed the name to The Skatalites. The Skatalites played on virtually every record made in Jamaica between 1963 and 1967, functioning as the equivalent of the studio bands at Motown and Stax in America. Their choppy sound became hugely influential and may have given ska its name. Unfortunately, Don Drummond never saw what became of his invention — in 1964 he murdered his girlfriend and died in an insane asylum in 1969, some say of natural causes, others say he was murdered by gangsters avenging his girlfriend's death, and some claim it was a government plot to suppress the powerful Jamaican music scene. "The SCA-TILites played on virtually every record made in Jamaica between 1963 and 1967."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Early Records Production
podcast.body: Coxsone Dodd produced the early records for The Skatalites. "Oh, and by the way, Cox and Dodd produced their early records."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: First Wave Ska Originator
podcast.body: The Skatalites were an originator of the "first wave" of Ska, a style born in Jamaica in the 1950s. Along with Desmond Dekker and Toots and the Maytals, these artists comprised the initial pioneers of the genre. "Those originators, Desmond Decker, Tutson the Maytaws, the Scott lights and so on, all from Jamaica comprised that first wave."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of the 2010s Part 4: The Revivals

podcast.title: Seminal Studio Band
podcast.body: The Skatalites were a "crack studio band" and appeared on numerous records produced in Jamaica between 1963 and 1967. Their choppy, danceable sounds significantly contributed to the spread of Ska, making them the equivalent of American studio outfits like The Wrecking Crew in Los Angeles or The Funk Brothers who played on Motown records. "The SCATALYTS were also a crack studio band and they appeared on so many records produced in Jamaica between 1963 and 1967."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Contribution to Ska Sound
xref.body: Don Drummond was a trombone player who helped give some of the early Ska music a darker sound. His band was initially called The Satellites, but by 1964, they became known as The Skatalites. "He was a trombone player who helped give some of this music a darker sound."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: First Wave Ska Originator
xref.body: Desmond Dekker was an originator of the "first wave" of Ska, a style born in Jamaica in the 1950s. Along with Toots and the Maytals and The Skatalites, these artists comprised the initial pioneers of the genre. "Those originators, Desmond Decker, Tutson the Maytaws, the Scott lights and so on, all from Jamaica comprised that first wave."
